## Customize the Post Meta

<https://docs.themegrill.com/colormag/docs/customize-the-post-meta/>

**Location**: Appearance → Customize → Content → Post Meta

Post Meta refers to the additional information of the post, such as Date, Author, Views, Comments, etc. ColorMag displays the post meta in Blog, category, and single post page and provides the following options:

## Enable

Switch the Toggle to the right area of each post meta to enable theelementson your site. Enabling the option will display the post meta elements above each content on your end.

Currently, with the ColorMag theme, you’ll get the following post elements:

- **Date** – It displays the post-published **Date**.

- **Author **– It displays the name of the post **Author**.

- **Views **– It shows the total **Views** of the post.

- **Comment** – It displays the number of **Comments** for that specific post.

- **Tags** – It displays the **Tag** added for the post.

- **Reading Time** – It shows the estimated **Reading Time** to read the post.

Enable Post Meta

**Disable the Edit Button **– Enabling the option will disable the **Edit** button on the post meta area.

Enable Edit Post Meta

## Date

It changes the Date Format styles appearing on the post meta area. It comes with two types listed below:

- **Style 1 **– It displays the Date format in Month, Date, and Year.

Date Format Style 1

- **Style 2** – It shows the Date format with respect to the time it was published earlier, i.e., 2 years ago and so on.

Date Format Style 2

## Text

With the ColorMag theme, you can change the color and typography of the post-meta elements.

- **Color** – It changes the **Color **of the post-meta elements.

Change Post Meta Color

- **Typography** – It changes the **Font-Size** of the post-meta elements.

Change Post Meta Font Size

## Customize Pagination

<https://docs.themegrill.com/colormag/docs/customize-pagination/>

**Location: **Appearance → Customize → Content → Blog → Pagination

Pagination is a way of splitting the contents of your site into multiple pages. ColorMag theme allows Pagination on the site with various ways of displaying it, which are explained below: **[Available in ColorMag Pro]**

## Enable

Switch the Toggle to the right area to enable the** Pagination** on your site. Enabling the option will display the Pagination on the blog page.

Enable Pagination

## Type

The theme provides three layouts for displaying the pagination feature on your end. The styles are explained below:

### Default

It displays the Pagination in the traditional style of the **Next** and **Previous **labels at the end of the blog page. Once this feature is enabled, you will see the labels, i.e., **Next Article **and **Previous Article**, at the end of the page.

Default Pagination

### Numbered

Number pagination displays the previous and next posts in the form of numbers. Once this feature is enabled, you will see numbers like 1,2,3… at the end of the page, redirecting you to the new page, i.e., back and forward.

Numbered Pagination

## Infinite Scroll in Blog Page **Pro**

<https://docs.themegrill.com/colormag/docs/infinite-scroll-in-blog-page/>

** Location:** Appearance → Customize → Content → Blog → Pagination → Infinite Scroll

Infinite loading is a technique that allows users to load all the posts on their blog page continuously in certain events, like while clicking a button or scrolling. **[Available in ColorMag Pro **].

ColorMag has an option for infinite loading to the post listing pages like blogs and categories. There are 2 ways of loading posts infinitely:

## **Button**

The Button is the method of Infinite Scroll where instead of loading the next page automatically, it is loaded on the user’s demand.

Under **Pagination → Type,** choose Infinite Scroll options. After that, under the **Style** section, choose **Button,** which will display a **Load More** button at the end of the blog page.

Clicking the Load More button will continuously load the post on the blog page.

Infinite Scroll Pagination with Button

## Scroll

The Scroll is a method of Infinite Scroll where the next post loads automatically upon scrolling the page.

Under **Pagination → Type,** choose Infinite Scroll options. After that, under the Style section, choose **Scroll**, which will display posts upon scrolling the blog page.

Infinite Scroll Pagination with Scroll

## Manage Excerpt Text and Length

<https://docs.themegrill.com/colormag/docs/manage-excerpt-text-and-length/>

**Location: **Appearance → Customize → Content → Blog → Excerpt

An excerpt refers to a summary of a post or article. The Excerpt is generated automatically by taking the first few lines of the Content. However, you can also manually create or customize the Excerpt for each post.

Sometimes on the blog page, you might prefer to show the full Content instead of the excerpt text or vice versa. ColorMag allows displaying either the Full Text or the excerpt text. **[Available in ColorMag Pro]**

## Excerpt

It displays the **Excerpt** (summary) of the posts. Upon choosing the option, you can set the **Length** and add additional **Text** to the Excerpt.

Display Excerpt Text

### Length **Pro**

By default, ColorMag limits excerpts’ Length to 20 words. You can increase or decrease the excerpt length on your preference.

Limit Excerpt Length

### More Text **Pro**

ColorMag theme allows you to add a specific text after the Excerpt. Generally, the Excerpt displays the first few words from your post content. However, the theme will enable you to add extra Content after the default excerpt text on the blog page. [**Available in ColorMag Pro **]

Under Content, you can add the Text required on **Change Excerpt More Text**. In the example below, we have added the “Hello ColorMag” text, which is now displayed after the default excerpt text on each post.

Adding More Excerpt Text

## Full Content

It displays the full content of the post.

Display Full Content

## Manage Blog Page Layout

<https://docs.themegrill.com/colormag/docs/manage-blog-page-layout/>

**Location: **Appearance → Customize → Content → Blog → General

As itsname suggests, a Blog page on a site refers to the page on a website that displays the **Blog Post**. The Layout on the blog page refers to how the blog posts are organized or rearranged.

Currenlty, the ColorMag theme provides two layouts for displaying the post on Blog/Category page: **[Available in ColorMag Pro]**

## Layout 1 **Pro**

Layout 1 displays the posts in the list layout. In the list layout, posts are displayed in a vertical series with one post after another and come in two styles, explained below:

- **Style 1 **– It displays the post in a single column with the feature image on the left and content on the right.

One-Column Blog Layout

- **Style 2** – It displays the post in a single column with the feature image in the center and content below it.

Full-Width Blog Layout

## Layout 2 **Pro**

Layout 1 displays the posts in the grid layout. In the grid layout, the posts are displayed in a series of rows and columns. It comes in two styles, explained below:

- **Style 1** – It displays the first post in full width with the other two post side by side.

Blog Page with Full Width and Two Posts Side by Side

- **Style 2** – It displays the post in multiple columns with a featured image on top and content below it. You can also choose the number of columns for displaying the post.

Blog Page with Grid Layout

---

## Customize AutoLoad Posts

<https://docs.themegrill.com/colormag/docs/customize-autoload-posts/>

**Location:** Appearance → Customize → Content → Single Post → AutoLoad Posts

With the ColorMag theme, the posts will be automatically loaded once the user reaches the bottom of the single post page. This will help user engagement by pulling the next posts into view when the reader reaches the bottom of the page.

It comes with the following option to manage the autoload posts on the single post page.

## Enable

Switch the Toggle to the right area to enable the** AutoLoads Posts **on your site. Enabling the option will display posts at the bottom of the single post page.

## Filter

The option allows you to choose between the posts that will be loaded. You can either choose the autoload posts to be the **Previous Posts **or **Next Posts**.

## Style

In the Style section, you can either choose the **Button** or **Scroll **option.

- Button – It displays a button **Load Post** at the end of the single post. Clicking the button will display the autoload posts.

- Scroll – It loads the posts automatically while scrolling the page below.

## Number of Posts

It allows you to choose the number of posts that you want to display as a autoload post.
